Co-director Arghya Lahiri on working with Naseeruddin Shah on Salman Rushdie's memoir 'Knife' for a stage adaptation
A dapting a devastating memoir about violence, recovery and resilience for the stage is no easy feat. It takes an actor of Naseeruddin Shah’s calibre to bring Salman Rushdie’s Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder , to life as a stage adaptation. Shah plays Rushdie in the play 27 Seconds for the Prithvi Festival and directs it too, with co-director Arghya Lahiri.

A dapting a devastating memoir about violence, recovery and resilience for the stage is no easy feat. It takes an actor of Naseeruddin Shah’s calibre to bring Salman Rushdie’s Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder , to life as a stage adaptation. Shah plays Rushdie in the play 27 Seconds for the Prithvi Festival and directs it too, with co-director Arghya Lahiri.
“Naseer reached out to Mr Rushdie directly for the rights,” says Lahiri, adding that the latter responded with great enthusiasm and understanding. “It was not difficult at all. I think it helps, of course, that it is Naseer,” he says. Rushdie has publicly spoken about his admiration for the actor.
The play, dramatised by Shah alongside veteran director Kaushik Sen, doesn’t attempt a word-for-word retelling of the book. Instead, it seeks to capture its emotional residue. “It’s like that Anthony Minghella (British filmmaker) quote about The Talented Mr. Ripley where he says, ‘You flush the book through your mouth and then you try and put down the taste that’s left’,” he says. What remains on stage is a meditation on resilience and freedom of expression. “My belief is that it allowed Mr Rushdie to draw a line under not just the attack, but the 33 years since the fatwa,” reflects Lahiri.
Directing with an icon like Shah might sound daunting, but Lahiri sees his role as simply being the “first audience” in the room. “I’m there to help him realise this vision,” he shares. Lahiri hopes Rushdie gets to see the play sometime. “If faith conspires that he gets to watch it, that would be wonderful indeed,” he signs off.
—The show will be staged on Nov. 2 and 3, and from Nov. 24-Dec. 6 at Prithvi Theatre, Mumbai, before heading to Chandigarh, Delhi and Bengaluru
